architecture_decisions: The architecture decision is to separate the server-owned validation command profile from the server-owned execution-environment capability that must satisfy it. This ensures that the validation and execution environments are distinct and can be independently managed and validated.
work_items: The work item is to create a new server-owned contract for the validation command policy and execution-environment policy. This will allow for the separation of the two contracts and ensure that they are independently managed and validated.
validations: The validation is to ensure that the validation command policy and execution-environment policy are separate server-owned contracts. This will allow for the separation of the two contracts and ensure that they are independently managed and validated.

AC-01: validate protected requirement — A finite server-owned registry binds each admitted validation profile to exactly one protected execution environment identity/digest. Repository/model/user/request values cannot override environment selection.

AC-02: validate protected requirement — The established Parallax/Python profile continues to resolve its current verified execution snapshot and all inherited protected execution behavior remains green.

AC-03: validate protected requirement — `dotnet-v1` resolves a separately pinned source-free execution environment whose server-owned absolute `dotnet` executable proves the released .NET 8 SDK version under deny-all networking.

AC-04: validate protected requirement — The one-time .NET environment provisioning path uses only fixed server-owned SDK identity/install commands and fixed Microsoft distribution domains, receives no repository/application/provider secrets or source, verifies the exact toolchain, snapshots it, and is absent/disabled from normal runtime after provisioning.

AC-05: validate protected requirement — Production deployment fails closed unless every runtime-admitted environment restores its exact snapshot and passes its fixed capability/version/source-free checks under deny-all networking.

AC-06: validate protected requirement — An OT Time-like candidate selecting `dotnet-v1` restores the .NET environment, records bounded environment identity/digest, performs bounded dependency PREPARE, and never uses the Python snapshot.

AC-07: validate protected requirement — BUILD/TEST/VERIFY against accepted lineage deterministically resolve the same validation-profile/environment policy identity as candidate validation; no lifecycle request can switch environments.

AC-08: validate protected requirement — Missing snapshot, snapshot mismatch, missing executable, wrong SDK version, or provider inability returns typed non-success evidence and performs no source-lineage acceptance, Git/provider mutation, deployment mutation, or fabricated lifecycle progress.

AC-09: validate protected requirement — Source-only and Vercel Preview delivery semantics, tenant/auth boundaries, provider scopes, single-writer source acceptance, immutable lineage, PREPARE package-domain authority, deny-all validation, and REVIEW ceiling do not regress.

AC-10: validate protected requirement — After exact production deployment, the QA-owned source-only Project bound to `github:Ryan9876/ot-time` progresses PLAN → IMPLEMENT → BUILD → TEST → VERIFY → REVIEW and the authenticated exact-lineage ZIP handoff verifies, without Vercel target deployment, Vercel repository-provider authorization, out-of-band source edit, owner impersonation, DB mutation, or authority widening.
risks: The risk is that the validation command policy and execution-environment policy will not be separate server-owned contracts. This could lead to inconsistencies and errors in the validation and execution environments.

critique: The bounded dependency PREPARE contract was not met, resulting in a `DEPENDENCY_PREPARATION_FAILED` error. The toolchain-probe and restore exit codes were absent, and both dependency output digests were the empty-string digest. The sandbox was successfully returned to deny-all. Production execution-snapshot preflight currently proves only the existing Parallax/Python offline dependencies and does not prove the .NET SDK exists. The remaining defect is therefore execution-environment readiness, not repository authority, delivery mode, profile selection, command…
